subject: RFI: Orchestrated migration matrix + safeguard / stepdown playbook
messages:
From: Jack Turner <jack.turner@omega-fin.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nate Alvarez <nate.alvarez@omega-fin.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: RFI follow-up: detailed migration/runbook requirements

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the high-level RFI packet. Procurement and our cloud ops team reviewed the section on cutover options and we need a granular migration matrix for our SOC/Board packet. Specifically we'd like: 1) a timeline broken into phases with objective gate criteria, 2) integration steps for the embedding / inference path into our existing pipeline, 3) a staged canary/fallback runbook if model latency/regression or GPU capacity issues occur, and 4) expected outage windows (if any) and a rollback decision tree.

Can Redwood provide a filled matrix and a playbook we can attach to the RFP addendum by next Friday (20 Nov)? We can route to our security reviewers as soon as we have it.

Appreciate it — Jack

--
Jack Turner
Head of Procurement
Omega Financial
jack.turner@omega-fin.com
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jack Turner <jack.turner@omega-fin.com>
Cc: Nate Alvarez <nate.alvarez@omega-fin.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: detailed migration/runbook requirements

Jack —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is an initial Implementation Matrix (rfi-responses-implementation-matrix.xlsx) and a 6-page Safeguard Playbook (redwood-migration-safeguard-playbook-v1.pdf). The matrix maps phases (Discovery, Staging, Canary, Production) to owners, verification gates, integration steps, and rollback criteria. The playbook includes:
- Canary traffic split recommendations (fixed % windows and automated rollback triggers),
- KV/prefix cache prewarm checklist,
- Model variant fallback mappings (quantized / smaller seq-length variants),
- Network dependency validation steps,
- Emergency stepdown commands and expected RTOs.

Quick notes:
- We assume a parallel staging environment with a copy of customer embeddings and a 1:1 request replay window for at least 48 hours before enabling traffic.
- Expected full production cutover (no-data-loss, incremental routing) can be completed in 3 business days after a successful canary, provided no regression signals.
- If GPU saturation occurs, the playbook prefers auto-fallback to a lower-cost quantized replica rather than queueing; rollback to prior routing is immediate on SLO breach.

If you'd like we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with your cloud ops team and our infra engineers next week. Linking the Drive doc for your reviewers: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2cRfi-implementation-matrix

Attachments: rfi-responses-implementation-matrix.xlsx, redwood-migration-safeguard-playbook-v1.pdf, network-topology-omega-dc.png

Best —
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: internal: Omega RFI - canary thresholds / metrics decision

Team —

Reviewed the matrix and playbook. A few operational clarifications we should agree internally before the walkthrough:

1) Canary windows: propose 3-stage windows (1%, 10%, 50%) each with at least 2 hours and automated metric checks (latency p95, error-rate, token drop rate). If any metric fails, immediate traffic rollback to previous variant. Fail criteria: p95 > 1.5x baseline OR error-rate > 0.5%.

2) KV/Persistent cache: recommend seeding top-5k prefixes and enabling prefix-hit monitoring. If prefix-hit < 70% during canary, escalate to product and pause rollout.

3) Capacity fallback: our routing supports per-route fallback to a quantized model with up to 20% quality degradation allowance; this must be explicitly signoff'd by Omega. We should capture this in the matrix L4: 'quality-sla-allowance'.

4) Network maintenance: include a pre-cutover test that simulates egress throttling and validates the graceful degradation hooks. Ops will run that test in staging.

I'll prepare language for the matrix for the metric thresholds. Laura — can you add the product-approval step and the stakeholder contact list to the matrix? Marissa — please prepare the HLD excerpt for the walkthrough.

- Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
Principal PM, Deployment & Runtime
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
From: Cynthia Park <cynthia.park@consult-ops.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jack Turner <jack.turner@omega-fin.com>
Cc: Nate Alvarez <nate.alvarez@omega-fin.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Question on rollback decision tree (clarification)

Hi Irene / Jack,

Thanks for the materials — our technical reviewers skimmed the playbook and have two clarifying requests before we finalize the addendum:

1) In the rollback decision tree (playbook page 3) you call out 'immediate rollback on SLO breach' — can you confirm the monitoring window? Is rollback immediate on a single anomalous spike or should it require 3 consecutive 1-minute checks?

2) For the model-variant fallback: are there signed metrics that define the expected semantic quality delta when falling back to quantized models? Our compliance team wants a documented measurement plan for quality drift detection.

If you could respond to both items and, if possible, add the monitoring-window language into the matrix we can close this item.

Thanks —
Cynthia
ConsultOps (3rd-party technical reviewer)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Cynthia Park <cynthia.park@consult-ops.com>, Jack Turner <jack.turner@omega-fin.com>
Cc: Nate Alvarez <nate.alvarez@omega-fin.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on rollback decision tree (clarification)

Cynthia —

Great questions. Short answers:

1) Monitoring window: we require 3 consecutive 1-minute checks (i.e., a 3-minute rolling window) before an automated rollback triggers. This avoids single-spike noise. The playbook has been updated (attached) to reflect that; see the new section 'Automated rollback confirmation: 3x1m'.

2) Quality delta measurement: we provide a two-tier measurement plan: a) offline similarity drift (embedding cosine drop) measured hourly during canary and b) live regression harness using a seed prompt set (100 prompts) run every canary window. We define an allowable semantic drift of <= 6% measured on our composite score (f1 + embedding-similarity normalized). Any drift > 6% flags a hold and requires product-owner sign-off. We will capture the exact scoring script in the Drive link and include a short note in the matrix.

I've uploaded the updated matrix and playbook with the monitoring-window language and the quality-measurement appendix. Next steps: schedule the 30-minute walkthrough (Irene + Aditya + Laura) with Omega's cloud ops and Cynthia next Tuesday 24 Nov, 10:00am PT. Jack — can you confirm?

Attachments: rfi-responses-implementation-matrix.xlsx (v2), redwood-migration-safeguard-playbook-v1.1.pdf

Best regards,
